rcomplex

rcomplex aligns gene co-expression networks across species, the way BLAST aligns sequences. Ortholog groups anchor the alignment. A pairwise alignment is a set of co-expressologs: ortholog pairs that keep their co-expression partners. A multiple alignment is a clique: genes in three or more species that are all co-expressed. An aligned block is a module. Every edge gets a score, an e-value, a q-value, an effect size and a power. The method extends ComPlEx (Netotea et al., 2014).

flowchart LR
  A[expression per species] --> H[harmonise: block or partition]
  H --> N[networks: top 3% of gene pairs]
  O[ortholog groups: hogs] --> C
  N --> C[co-expressologs: edges]
  C --> Q[cliques: multiple alignment]
  C --> M[modules: aligned blocks]
  Q --> T[tiers and clades]
  C --> Z[nulls and power]

Install 

devtools::install_github("paliocha/rcomplex")

You need a C++23 compiler and GNU make. OpenMP is optional.

Run

Give rcomplex() one expression object per species, a table of hogs, and optional clades. The example uses four Pooideae grasses that ship with the package.

library(rcomplex)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
se <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "pooideae_vignette.rds",
                          package = "rcomplex"))
leaf <- lapply(se[c("BDIS", "BSYL", "HVUL", "HJUB")],
               function(s) s[, s$tissue == "leaf"])
hogs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(leaf), function(s) data.frame(
  species = s, gene = rownames(leaf[[s]]), hog = rowData(leaf[[s]])$hog)))

Then run the driver:

clades <- list(annual = c("BDIS", "HVUL"), perennial = c("BSYL", "HJUB"))
res <- rcomplex(leaf, hogs, clades = clades, seed = 1)
#> gene_clique_graph: 1245 genes collapsed into 577 twin classes; cliques
#>   carry multiplicity
res
#> rcomplex: 4 species, 1,500 hogs, 3 tiers
#>   BDIS  1,935 genes  20 samples  density 0.03  r >= 0.35
#>   BSYL  1,967 genes  20 samples  density 0.03  r >= 0.33
#>   HVUL  1,925 genes  20 samples  density 0.03  r >= 0.29
#>   HJUB  3,983 genes  20 samples  density 0.03  r >= 0.28
#>   edges 33,575 tested, 10,387 called at q < 0.1
#>   cliques 3,125 distinct (17,653 with paralog copies): complete_conserved 1,977, partial_present    68, unclassified 1,080

Use summary(res) for the tier table, write_rcomplex(res, "out/") to save the tables, and rcomplex(networks = ...) for networks built elsewhere. Pass block for a designed experiment. Pass modules = TRUE for modules. Pass null = TRUE to rerun with hog labels shuffled among genes of the same expression level.

The quickstart runs this example step by step.

Output

res$edges has one row per ortholog pair in each species pair.

Column Meaning
gene1, gene2 The two orthologs.
hog Their ortholog group.
score -log2(p). Higher is stronger.
evalue n_tests * p: pairs this strong expected by chance.
q_value False discovery rate.
effect_size Fold enrichment of shared partners.
power Chance to call the pair if it were conserved.

res$classification has one row per clique and its tier.

Three pitfalls

  1. Few samples. The density threshold keeps the top 3% of gene pairs at any sample size. At 20 samples that means weak correlations. Read r >= in the header. A value near 0.3 means the network holds a lot of chance correlation.
  2. Density. A looser density adds edges and noise. A tighter one removes true edges. Run density_sweep() and keep the calls that survive.
  3. The p-value floor. A permutation p-value cannot fall below 1 / (n_perm + 1). Trait tests over few species have a higher floor. Run pvalue_resolution() before you trust a q-value.
